title: Reinforcement learning to design near-perfect acoustic absorbers
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is proposed as a strategy for the multi-objective design of Helmholtz resonators with near-perfect acoustic absorption. The approach formulates resonator design as a sequential decision-making problem in which geometrical parameters are iteratively updated to balance competing objectives, including resonator volume, resonance frequency, and acoustic reflection. A Q-learning algorithm based on a neural network is developed to explore the design space and identify non-dominated solutions, providing a Pareto front of optimal configurations. The acoustic response is evaluated using a transfer matrix method that incorporates viscothermal losses and acoustic end corrections. Three representative designs are subsequently investigated using full-wave finite element simulations, showing good agreement in their absorption and reflection spectra and validating the accuracy of the reduced-order model. Finally, one optimized resonator is fabricated by three-dimensional printing and experimentally characterized in an impedance tube. The measured absorption coefficient reaches approximately 95\% near the resonance frequency, in agreement with the numerical predictions. These results demonstrate the potential of reinforcement learning for the automated design of compact acoustic absorbers and establish a computationally efficient framework combining multi-objective optimization, numerical modelling, and experimental validation.

title: Sparse, admissible and interpretable: discovery of isotropic limit surfaces with extended invariant libraries, physically gated mixtures of experts, and end-to-end structural identification
summary: Choosing and fitting a limit surface, a yield or failure criterion, to multiaxial strength tests is a model-selection problem with physical side conditions. The equivalent stress concept provides a catalogue of criteria with admissibility conditions: convexity, a unique surface definition, explicit solvability, and bounds on inelastic Poisson ratios. We recast the task as sparse, constrained, differentiable model discovery and compare three representations. The first is a library of invariant monomials I1^a q^m r3^c containing classical criteria as sparse members. The second extends this library by trigonometric Lode-angle terms, restricted by isotropy to cosine modes, and Podgorski-Bigoni-Piccolroaz (PBP) atoms with learnable shape parameters. The third is a mixture of convex gauge experts using either a competition (smooth-maximum) or direction gate with hard-concrete and Gumbel-softmax sparsity. A ray-wise first-root definition gives explicit solvability and an exactly differentiable objective. Convexity and absence of re-entrant branches are differentiable penalties for the libraries and hold by construction for the competition gate. That gate acts as a physically motivated regime selector between mechanisms. Under stated assumptions its responsibilities are the share of failure probability in Weibull statistics, the share of dissipation in Koiter's multi-surface flow rule, and a Boltzmann weight in Gibbs principles. In synthetic benchmarks, the extended library recovers truths like Mohr-Coulomb and PBP surfaces within 1% error. We analyse five experimental datasets: two PMI foams, PA6, concrete, and TSSA in Hencky-strain space. A sharp Lode function matters more than many terms. With PBP atoms, concrete data are fitted with a fourfold lower error. End-to-end identification from notched-bar loads via differentiable finite elements removes nominal-stress mapping bias.

title: Establishing Standards for Assessment and Reporting of SNSPD Performance
summary: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) can be made sensitive to single photons with near-unity detection efficiency, ultra-low dark-count rates, and sub-nanosecond timing jitter over a broad wavelength range. However, many studies report data inconsistently, often emphasizing a single performance metric without considering overall device performance. This inconsistent data reporting limits the field, as it makes it difficult to determine which device characteristics are most important. Different applications require functionalities that may conflict with one another; for example, longer-wavelength operation may require lower operating temperatures. Moreover, there is no universally accepted metric for defining the figures of merit of an SNSPD. In this work, we amass a dataset representing the state of the art of SNSPD fabrication, including operating temperature, operating wavelength, photon count rates (PCR), and dark count rates (DCR). We fit the PCR curves and suggest using the saturation plateau length to gauge the SNSPD's sensitivity. We then fit the DCR and compare the PCR and DCR. Using this approach, we establish a quantitative framework to determine the optimal biasing condition for a given device and to determine the device's sensitivity at that optimal biasing condition, enabling meaningful comparisons across disparate devices. Additionally, we offer concrete benchmarks for measuring device performance.

title: High-directivity pulsed beams for effective power and information transfer
summary: A vector spherical wave expansion (VSWE) is used to engineer an elemental multipole source whose radiated field is a superdirective, extremely unidirectional (SDEU) needle beam. It is proved analytically and confirmed numerically that the element attains Harrington's normal-directivity value along its beam axis. Its radiated field is linearly polarized with an azimuthally symmetric magnitude; its back lobe vanishes identically in the far field. The unidirectional behavior is quantified at any finite far-field radius by a closed-form front-to-back ratio, obtained from an exact per-degree cancellation of the electric and magnetic multipole contributions in the backward direction. Uniform circular arrays (UCAs) of these elements inherit the SDEU behavior. Driving the arrays with zero-area pulses (ZAPs) transfers the frequency-domain performance intact into the time domain. It is shown that whether the radiated energy beam is narrower or wider than the corresponding intensity beam is decided by a single property of the radiated waveform, not by the size of the radiating aperture. A simple single-cycle ZAP is used to quantify the performance of the UCAs; its energy beam is the narrower one. The same criterion is shown to govern the focal spot of near-field-focused pulse-driven arrays. A custom-designed intensity-enhancement (IE) ZAP is introduced that raises the focal intensity by almost 200-fold over a narrow-band reference while producing a focal spot more than ten times smaller in both the axial and transverse directions, deeply subwavelength with respect to its own effective wavelength. It is demonstrated that these stunning IE results are produced simply with an array of pulse-excited Huygens dipole sources. These results identify the pulse shape, rather than the aperture, as the design variable that governs localized electromagnetic energy and information delivery.

title: Selecting Person Segmentation Models for Real-Time Video Call Backgrounds on the CPU
summary: Background blur and background replacement are now normal parts of a video call. Many open models and open source pipelines can do this, but it is hard to know which one to pick. Speed, edge quality and license all matter, and they are often reported on different hardware, or not reported at all. In this work we ran 20 setups on the same laptop CPU, with the same 640x480 frames and the same output view. The setups are 15 open models and 5 complete open source pipelines. We measured frames per second on a test clip and on a live webcam, compared the masks on a public domain portrait and on three video call photos with a raised hand, one of them a close front camera view, and recorded the license of every model. The fastest setups reach more than 40 frames per second on a laptop CPU, while the slowest, a high detail model for still images, needs several seconds per frame. A few setups give clean edges and still run in real time. We also found that the runtime library and the steps around the model can change the speed by several times. Based on these results we give a guide that tells the reader which model to choose for a given need, such as a weak laptop, the best hair edges, a closed source product, or people behind the speaker.

title: AI-assisted search for self-compressing gigawatt subcycle field waveforms
summary: We explore the physics behind pulse self-compression to high-power subcycle field waveforms and search for the optimal regimes of such compression over the parameter space as laid out by multimode nonlinear dynamics of ultrashort laser pulses in gas-filled hollow fibers. With the pertinent physical criteria for pulse contrast and no pulse breakup formalized as operational stopping rules, a radical speedup of such search is achieved by delegating its tedious preliminary stages to generative pretrained transformer models. The precise adjustment of self-compression dynamics vis-a-vis the desired compressed pulse output is, however, not yet delegable to AI agents, as the criteria for such search are still largely subjective, operating with fine aspects of subcycle field structure, not yet formalizable as clear search-stopping instructions. An ultimate precision in such subcycle field engineering is attainable via a management of field-phase-sensitive nonlinear processes, enabling pulse self-compression to high-power subcycle field waveforms and opening paths toward fiber-optic attosecond lightwave engineering.

title: Metasurfaces with Anisotropic Electric and Magnetic Conductivities: Parameter Retrieval for Arbitrary Incidence and Polarization
summary: Metasurfaces come in a great variety of unit cell geometries and material composition. A common approach for describing them relies on retrieving effective surface parameters (e.g., electric and magnetic conductivities) from plane-wave scattering data. Conventional retrieval methods are often limited to isotropic unit cells, a uniform host material, or lead to increased complexity by requiring reflection and transmission coefficients from both sides of the metasurface. Here, we derive analytical expressions for the equivalent surface conductivities of an electrically- and magnetically-polarizable anisotropic metasurface under oblique plane-wave incidence with arbitrary polarization. The proposed formulation does not require bidirectional scattering information, thus simplifying the process especially in experimental studies. The method is validated through representative electric and magnetic meta-atoms at microwave and THz frequencies, respectively. Their ability for polarization conversion is demonstrated and discussed relying on the physical insight provided by the retrieved anisotropic conductivities. In addition, we present the inverse expressions for calculating the reflection and transmission coefficients from known surface conductivity tensors, which can prove useful for metasurface synthesis and radiation problems.

title: Development of Sapphire-Based Solid-State Neutron Detectors for Fusion Environments
summary: Single-crystal diamond is the reference solid-state technology for fast neutron detection in fusion devices. Despite this, its complex manufacturing increases their costs and puts limitations on their geometry. Moreover, the limits in their long-term stability and their behaviour in harsh environments further constraint its applications. Synthetic sapphire (Al2O2) is a promising alternative as a solid state detector material: it is available in large, low-cost wafers and features both a wider bandgap and a higher displacement energy compared to diamond. Despite this, it has so far received little-to-no attention as a neutron detector. This work presents the first steps of a development programme for sapphire-based fast neutron detectors. Eight prototypes with 4.5 x 4.5 mm2 and 9 x 9 mm2 active areas and 625 um thickness were fabricated from commercial wafers with Al-Si electrodes and coupled to different electronic configurations. All prototypes detected 5.47 MeV alpha particles from a 241Am source, confirming the viability of both the fabrication process and the use of sapphire as an active material. The small signals (30-40 mV over a peak-to-peak noise of about 8 mV) and the count rate increasing with bias indicate that sapphires will require higher electric fields than the ones experimented in the work (up to about 2.5 kV). Geant4 simulations were also used to estimate the response of a sapphire detector to 14.06 MeV (DT) neutrons, highlighting the perspectives of the detector as a fusion diagnostic.

title: One Block Is Enough: LoopMR for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
summary: Deep-learning unrolled networks are the leading approach to accelerated MRI reconstruction. State-of-the-art models such as PromptMR+ learn a distinct block for every cascade, so their size grows with the number of cascades. Sharing one block across iterations avoids adding parameters, but earlier shared-weight models typically used a tiny block and produced worse images than models with distinct weights. Therefore, it remained unclear whether weight sharing itself or the choice of block was the problem. Recent advances in looped transformers, which reuse the same block across layers, show that they can match or outperform their distinct-weight counterparts on several tasks. Motivated by this, we propose LoopMR, which reuses a single Restormer block at every iteration as its core. Besides the current image estimate, the block receives data-consistency inputs and latent images. On four datasets covering the brain (CC359), knee (fastMRI), heart (CMRxRecon2023) and carotid (in-house), LoopMR significantly outperforms E2E-VarNet, PromptMR and PromptMR+ in PSNR and SSIM at every acceleration factor (p < 0.01), with about 1/9 of PromptMR+'s parameters (10.3M versus 92.9M). It also keeps its lead at unseen acceleration factors and on an unseen dataset. With our transformer block, the shared model matches or outperforms its distinct-weight counterpart at 6, 12 and 24 iterations. At a fixed number of iterations, shared transformer blocks match or outperform their distinct-weight versions, while shared CNN blocks perform worse. These results suggest that looping one well-chosen block can outperform stacking distinct cascades in MRI reconstruction, with a fraction of the parameters.

title: Integrated optical isolators enabled by 2D semiconductors via spin-momentum locking
summary: Integrated optical isolators based on spin-momentum locking hold great potential for protecting photonic integrated circuits from unwanted reflections. Currently, the most common implementations are magneto-optical isolators that require an externally applied magnetic field. Nevertheless, a wide range of nonreciprocal effects remains to be exploited in alternative material platforms. Although the majority of these effects induce changes to the propagation of light as a function of its polarization, they can be directly connected to the propagation direction through spin-momentum locking. We employ a computational approach to investigate various designs of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors, studying the influence of their geometry and optical properties on the device performance. Additionally, we propose a novel concept for an all-optical isolator based on spin-valley polarization and optically tunable magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers. Our results establish 2D semiconductors as an advanced platform for integrated nonreciprocal devices, enabling functionalities that are difficult to achieve with conventional magneto-optical materials like all-optical operation.

title: The physical design of the superfluid helium-4 UCN source at CSNS
summary: Ultracold neutrons (UCN) play a crucial role in fundamental physics research, enabling investigations into new sources of CP violation, neutron lifetime measurements, and the exploration of non-Newtonian forces. However, these experiments are often limited by the intensity of UCN sources. The China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) is developing a UCN source utilizing superfluid helium-4 at Beamline 12. This paper focuses on enhancing UCN density and total UCN number by analyzing various parameters that impact the UCN system, including the influence of different wavelengths of cold neutrons, incident beam size, converter length, wall and reflector materials, extraction method, extraction guide radius, and guide material composition. A preliminary design of the UCN source at CSNS is presented based on this analysis. For a Be-coated converter, the predicted saturated UCN density is 315 UCN/cm^3, with a UCN production rate of 12,055 UCN/s and an extraction efficiency of 84%, yielding approximately 1.3 x 10^6 extracted UCNs per cycle in accumulation mode. The UCN source design presented in this study forms part of the overall physical design of the Neutron Physics and Application Spectrometer at CSNS, which successfully passed its physical design review on March 25, 2025.

title: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models
comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Medical Reasoning with Vision Language Foundation Models (Med-Reasoner). 16 pages including NeurIPS checklist, 1 figure, 5 tables
summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) are compared mainly by accuracy averaged across findings, a summary that can hide complete failure on a single diagnosis. We audit five open medical VLMs (MedGemma-4B, Lingshu-7B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and MedVLM-R1) on 6,048 ChestX-ray14 questions balanced by sex, age, finding, and label. On the 432 pneumothorax-positive X-rays, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL detect zero cases while MedGemma and Lingshu detect 38% and 67% of the same images. The two failing models answer "no" to all 864 pneumothorax cases (balanced accuracy 0.500, chance), yet produce fluent, anatomically specific explanations that name the signs of a collapsed lung and then deny them, with no hedge or abstention. This failure is not an artifact of prompting, image resolution, label ambiguity, or model scale. It persists across four prompt formats, at native resolution, and on single-label cases. A within-model control shows the same forced prompt gives HuatuoGPT 79% recall on nodule but only 6% on pneumothorax. It survives a tenfold scale increase (Qwen2.5-VL-72B detects 4%) and replicates on SIIM-ACR, an independent dataset with radiologist-drawn masks, where the failing models detect 0 of 432 confirmed pneumothoraces, including 0 of the 144 largest lesions. Reading the models' logits and internal states shows this is not blindness. The two failing models are highly confident yet no better than chance and a linear probe recovers pneumothorax from their hidden representations even where recall is zero, so the finding is represented internally but suppressed at the output. Aggregate accuracy therefore cannot establish that a medical VLM can see a given finding, because a model that misses one can still describe it convincingly. Reporting per-finding recall and specificity on balanced cases is needed to tell the difference.

title: A Field-Deployable 2U Ultra-Stable Laser with Sub-Hertz Linewidth Based on Optoelectronic Oscillator Locking
summary: Compact, high-performance ultra-stable lasers that can operate outside the laboratory remain a long-standing goal. Here we report, to our knowledge, the most compact field-deployable ultra-stable laser, packaged in a standard 2U rack chassis. It is stabilized to a 50 mm-long, 19 mL optical reference cavity with low vibration sensitivity by optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) locking, an approach particularly suited to compact, transportable systems. The laser delivers an integrated linewidth of about 0.42 Hz and a fractional frequency stability of about 5E-15 at 1 s averaging time (about 2.2E-15 at 0.4 s). Measured phase noise approaches the cavity thermal-noise limit below 100 Hz and the theoretical OEO-locking limit from 100 Hz to 100 kHz. The system volume is roughly one quarter of the volume of previously reported integrated, transportable ultra-stable lasers of comparable performance, making it well suited for field applications in time-frequency metrology, quantum technologies, and environmental sensing.

title: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
summary: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices. Here, we demonstrate scalable, ultra-bright, and highly uniform SiC quantum nanophotonic arrays. By combining a self-aligned fabrication process with localized oxygen ion implantation, we deterministically position PL5 and PL6 centers at the exact center of 4H-SiC nanopillars. This architecture yields record-high photon count rates of $\sim$1 Mcps (PL5) and $\sim$2 Mcps (PL6), establishing a new benchmark for SiC color centers while maintaining near-identical brightness across the array. Furthermore, we apply these devices to nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), successfully demonstrating external nanoscale nuclear-spin detection. These results establish our SiC nanopillars as robust building blocks for scanning quantum probes and scalable sensor networks.

title: Development of millikelvin scintillation photodetectors with CUPID
comment: 6 pages, 9 figures, to be submitted to NIM-A (NDIP26 conference proceedings)
summary: CUPID is a next-generation tonne-scale cryogenic experiment that will search for the neutrinoless double beta decay $(0νββ)$ of $^{100}$Mo. It will be located at the Gran Sasso National Laboratory (Italy) and will employ the cryogenic calorimetric technique to reconstruct the energy deposited in Li$_{2}$MoO$_{4}$ crystals, in which the isotope of interest is embedded. Preliminary measurements have been performed with the CUPID VSTT (Vertical Slice Test Tower), a prototype tower designed to test the detectors' response and the apparatus' mechanical and thermal stability. In addition, a key objective was to demonstrate the improved performance of germanium-based cryogenic light detectors. In CUPID, light detection is used for both particle identification and pile-up rejection. Li$_{2}$MoO$_{4}$ is a scintillating crystal, enabling particle identification by exploiting the dependence of light yield on particle type. This requires collecting the Li$_{2}$MoO$_{4}$ scintillation light, peaking at $\sim$600 nm, with a $\sim$300 $μ$m-thick high-purity germanium wafer placed next to the crystal. The wafer is also equipped with concentric Al electrodes biased at a few tens of volts. This bias improves the signal-to-noise ratio by an order of magnitude thanks to the Neganov-Trofimov-Luke effect. This work presents preliminary results on the performance of the VSTT light detectors and of its Optical Injection System.

title: Coarse-to-Fine 3D MRI Reconstruction via Resolution-Agnostic Neural Operators
summary: Deep-learning-based 3D MRI reconstruction is limited in practice by the GPU memory and compute cost of full-volume training; 3D acquisitions are thus most often reconstructed by 2D models applied slice-by-slice and then stacked, which ignores through-plane (stacking-axis) structure. We reconstruct in full 3D and ask whether a model can be trained at low resolution (fast and memory-feasible) yet deployed at higher resolution. This coarse-to-fine strategy needs reliable cross-resolution performance, but standard networks are resolution-specific and degrade substantially when evaluated outside the training setting. We therefore use resolution-agnostic neural operators (NOs) and propose KIR-NO (k-space-to-Image Reconstruction Neural Operator), a discretization-agnostic framework for accelerated 3D MRI reconstruction. KIR-NO is trained with full backpropagation on low-resolution volumes and applied zero-shot to higher-resolution volumes at inference. Its core building block is a 3D neural operator based on discrete-continuous convolutions: convolutional filters are parameterized in a continuous basis and sampled at arbitrary voxel resolutions while preserving the local inductive bias of convolution. KIR-NO integrates these learned operators with physics-based consistency: a k-space neural-operator head first refines the undersampled Fourier measurements, and image-space neural-operator cascades then refine the reconstruction through interleaved data-consistency updates. Across 3D knee and brain MRI benchmarks, KIR-NO improves over classical and CNN baselines: it improves over a state-of-the-art 3D CNN by 2.2 dB PSNR at half resolution under 4x acceleration on SKM-TEA, with gains persisting at 8x and 16x. These results show that resolution-agnostic operators make coarse-to-fine 3D MRI reconstruction - cheap low-resolution training with high-resolution deployment - practical across anatomies.

title: Analytic T-Matrix Formalism for Helmholtz Resonators
summary: We develop an analytic T-matrix formalism for two-dimensional circular acoustic Helmholtz resonators with thin rigid walls. The central idea is to use an aperture projection operator to obtain a compact expression for the T-matrix with explicit coefficients describing coupling and decoupling between external fields and cavity resonances. An equivalent formulation providing much faster convergence uses an aperture-to-Fourier map and an edge-adapted basis for the aperture flux. The method extends directly to multiple apertures of arbitrary angular widths and positions. The calculated scattering spectra agree with full-wave numerical simulations. For single- and double-aperture resonators, we decompose the T-matrix into even and odd parts under inversion to identify the channels associated with Willis coupling. We show how internal losses enable direction-dependent scattering and absorption when inversion symmetry is broken, while reciprocity ensures equal extinction for opposite incidence. Finally, we show how shifting the expansion origin redistributes radiation among multipole channels, enabling more compact T-matrix representations.

title: Xenon energy-deposition widths in silicon: measurements and Geant4 comparisons
summary: Energy-deposition fluctuations determine the isotope-separation capability of multilayer silicon detectors. We measure the central peak widths of $^{124}$Xe signals in 300- and 675-micrometre silicon layers at incident energies of approximately 152-274 MeV per nucleon and compare them with Geant4 11.4.0 electromagnetic option 4 (emopt4) and a calculation with explicit charge exchange. In the 300-micrometre detector, the emopt4 relative width of 1.844% exceeds the unselected experimental width of 1.407% by 31% and the selected width of 1.060% by 74%. For the 675-micrometre detector, selection windows around the downstream-signal peak, each approximately ten fitted first-plane standard deviations wide, give experimental upper estimates of 0.66-0.74%, compared with emopt4 predictions of 1.01-1.24%. Explicit charge-state transport gives widths of 0.889-0.932% for the thinner layer, depending on the incident charge distribution, and 0.59-0.63% for the thicker layer. These predictions are consistent with the experimental upper estimates, while emopt4 overestimates the widths for both thicknesses throughout the studied energy interval.

title: Interpreting Selective-Review Coverage for Head-and-Neck Auto-Contours
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027
summary: Selective-review systems aim to reduce human review by passing candidates predicted to be low risk. However, coverage (the fraction passed) can be misleading when measurements needed to interpret risk are unavailable. We separate structural evaluability (a nonempty mask with all required measurements available), computational-endpoint status, and pass-or-review decisions using archived Mayo records and controlled OpenKBP analyses. In 3,968 Mayo records, all 1,167 recorded empty predictions (predicted target-organ masks containing zero voxels despite nonempty reference masks) were endpoint-negative and passed both modules, accounting for approximately 76% of each pass set. In a held-out OpenKBP test, a logistic-regression router achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.833 and average precision of 0.449 but passed all 544 non-evaluable candidates, including 542 prespecified empty-mask controls and 2 erosions that became empty. A structural gate removed those passes without changing scores or the threshold, preserved all evaluable passes, and assigned 98.71% of endpoint-positive candidates to review. Under the original preprocessing and in patient-disjoint development evaluation, a router trained only on evaluable candidates and a router modeling an unavailable state likewise passed no non-evaluable candidates, with similar evaluable discrimination and at least 99.0% of endpoint-positive candidates assigned to review in pooled outer-fold predictions. These results show that coverage should be interpreted jointly with candidate eligibility, endpoint scope, missingness handling, and routing rules; they do not establish clinical validity, deployment safety, or natural-failure prevalence.

title: Ultrahigh-speed digital holography reveals blood flow beneath the skin
summary: Laser Doppler holography (LDH) leverages ultrahigh-speed digital holography to reveal blood-flow signals in vessels beneath the skin of the closed eyelid and around the eye. We demonstrate this in one volunteer using recordings acquired at approximately 16,000 frames/s under 10~mW of diffuse near-infrared illumination. Numerical Fresnel reconstruction and principal-component filtering reveal branching vascular patterns. These results extend an ocular imaging system to blood-flow visualization beneath the skin without requiring elaborate immobilization procedures.

title: Development and characterization of monolithic sensors with internal gain in a 110 nm CMOS process
summary: This paper presents the optimization and characterization of a Monolithic Active Pixel Sensor with internal gain implemented in the 110 nm CMOS process from LFoundry. This work, carried out within the framework of the latest ARCADIA production run, reports on the characterization of sensors with an optimized gain layer. Improvements over earlier prototypes, including substrate current reduction via guard-ring connection, are briefly discussed. Both laboratory and in-beam measurements are presented. Using soft X-rays from a 55Fe source, both the pixel response and the noise performance are analyzed. In addition, laser measurements demonstrate an electronic jitter ranging from 20 to 40 ps for a signal amplitude corresponding to one minimum ionizing particle (MIP). Finally, the results from several test beam campaigns are described, showing the signal amplitude, gain and time resolution of sensors with different doping profiles of the gain layer evaluated with MIPs. A time resolution of about 78 ps was measured in the optimal condition of bias voltage and electronics configuration. The results demonstrate that monolithic CMOS sensors with internal gain can achieve promising timing performance at ambient temperature, highlighting their strong potential for next-generation precision timing applications.

title: Supervision-Aware Evaluation of MedGemma for Reference-Assisted Radiotherapy Contour Ranking
comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027
summary: Radiotherapy contour ranking can support quality assurance, but vision-language model (VLM) gains may reflect supervision, score construction, available inputs, or representation access. We evaluated frozen MedGemma 1.5 in a single-institution study, a 12-patient held-out HaN-Seg test, five-fold cross-fitting on 30 non-test HaN-Seg patients, and transfer without refitting to 120 SegRap2023 patients. On held-out HaN-Seg, a supervised readout of the final prompt state exceeded a supervised readout of the model's yes/no output probabilities by +0.3047 pooled average precision (AP; 95% patient-bootstrap interval [+0.2822, +0.3269]); the advantage persisted against a parameter-count-matched nonlinear control. A readout of projected visual tokens exceeded the final-state readout in cross-fitting and transfer (+0.0706 AP averaged equally across patients on SegRap; 95% interval [+0.0607, +0.0804]), while a structured panel-feature readout remained competitive with visual tokens. The anatomy-conditioned readout did not demonstrate an advantage over the native-feature comparator. These results motivate visual-token and structured-feature controls in medical-imaging VLM evaluations; outcomes were computational or synthetic, not clinical acceptability.

title: Laser-induced damage threshold of periodic plasmonic metasurfaces
summary: Plasmonic metasurfaces enable strong nonlinear optical responses due to sub-wavelength field confinement, yet their performance is fundamentally limited by low laser-induced damage thresholds (LIDT). Here, we present a comprehensive experimental and numerical study of the interplay between surface lattice resonances (SLRs), second-harmonic generation (SHG), and LIDT in periodic gold nanobar metasurfaces. Angle-resolved measurements reveal that excitation of SLRs at the fundamental wavelength strongly enhances SHG efficiency while simultaneously reducing the LIDT. In contrast, excitation of an SLR at the second-harmonic wavelength does not affect the damage threshold, allowing the SHG signal to be maximized. Our findings establish a fundamental trade-off between nonlinear efficiency and optical robustness and provide design guidelines for optimizing periodic plasmonic metasurfaces for high-power nonlinear applications.

title: CCGeant4: charge-state-resolved transport and energy-loss fluctuations of relativistic heavy ions in Geant4
summary: CCGeant4 models energy-loss fluctuations of heavy ions in Geant4, accounting for both charge exchange and relativistic corrections to electron scattering beyond the first Born approximation. We use GLOBAL cross sections for electron capture and loss, ATIMA equilibrium stopping powers and charge-dependent delta-electron spectra calculated from the Dirac equation in a frozen-shell potential. The package also supports tabulated elastic ion-nucleus scattering. The silicon example includes interference between Coulomb and nuclear scattering amplitudes. We compare charge evolution with GLOBAL and energy-loss spectra with MOCADI for matched beams and targets. Experimental comparisons cover the energy-loss measurements of Weick et al. and several measurements of energy deposited by xenon ions in silicon. For uranium at 800 MeV/u, the energy-loss variances from our Dirac configuration agree with the screened-ion calculations of Weick et al. to within 4% in Be, Al and Pb. Both calculations lie within the reported experimental uncertainties for all three targets, while calculated bismuth spectra in silver are narrower than measured. Calculations in thin silicon layers show that delta-electron escape can make deposited-energy distributions substantially narrower than primary-ion energy-loss distributions, highlighting the importance of secondary-electron transport for detector-response modelling. The distribution includes the Geant4 source patch, the transport tables and their converters, and a runnable example.

title: HR-NVC++: Unified Ultra-High-Resolution Neural Video Coding with Confidence-Guided Spatial-Temporal Cues
summary: Ultra-high-resolution neural video coding (NVC) remains challenging because temporal correspondence becomes increasingly unreliable as spatial resolution increases. Although recent neural B-frame codecs have improved bi-directional temporal prediction, complex motion and fine-grained structures still lead to unreliable temporal references, while spatial information of the current frame remains underexploited. In this work, we propose HR-NVC++, a unified ultra-high-resolution NVC approach that supports both fidelity-oriented and perceptual-quality-oriented compression with a shared spatial-temporal context. The context integrates bi-directional temporal cues with complementary spatial information: confidence-guided fusion adaptively balances the forward and backward temporal cues according to their estimated correspondence reliability, while a spatial complement branch enriches regions that temporal references fail to explain. The resulting context serves as a common basis for two compression modes. Built upon this shared context, the fidelity mode retains entropy-based latent coding for pixel-accurate compression, whereas the perceptual mode removes additional latent coding and performs reconstruction directly from the context. This design demonstrates that a sufficiently informative spatial-temporal context already carries the dominant content required for perceptually favorable reconstruction, allowing different compression objectives to share the same contextual representation. Extensive experiments on UVG-4K and JVET Class A1/A2 show that HR-NVC++ achieves an average PSNR BD-rate saving of 13.01% over the H.266/VVC reference model VTM-13.2 under the random access configuration, while delivering substantially better perceptual quality and temporal consistency than existing neural video codecs.

title: Gradient-Free Inverse Design of 3D Nanophotonic Devices Using the Level-Set-Method
summary: Advances in 3D nanophotonic additive manufacturing enable increasingly complex, almost free-form devices for manipulating light at sub-wavelength scales. Extending nanophotonic designs into three dimensions introduces additional degrees of freedom. Exploiting this freedom requires inverse-design methods that can efficiently navigate this large design space while accommodating fabrication constraints. Here, we combine gradient-free optimization with the level-set method (LSM) to provide such an approach for 3D additive manufacturing. Representing the 3D geometry as a level set constructed from Gaussian radial basis functions retains substantial geometric freedom with only a few hundred design variables. This compact representation makes gradient-free optimization practical for fully 3D nanophotonic devices, eliminating the need for adjoint calculations. This unlocks the use of any Maxwell solver or auxiliary algorithms that should express fabrication constraints for which the required derivatives are unavailable or impractical to obtain, and enables embarrassingly parallel workflows. Consequently, binary fabrication requirements, such as structural connectivity, can be rigorously enforced, avoiding the differentiable approximations commonly used in gradient-based optimization. Here, we demonstrate the combination of the gradient-free LSM with a connected-component analysis algorithm to enforce the structural integrity of the design. We demonstrate the applicability of the gradient-free LSM by optimizing a Y-splitter while strictly enforcing the structural integrity of the material and the void in the design.

title: Characterization of a Large-Area HRPPD MCP-PMT Coupled to LYSO for TOF-PET
comment: 8 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
summary: Large-area microchannel-plate photomultipliers (MCP-PMTs) such as the High-Rate Picosecond Photon Detector (HRPPD) are attractive for time-of-flight positron emission tomography (TOF-PET). They offer excellent single-photon time resolution, low dark count rate, and large monolithic active areas. However, the coincidence time resolution (CTR) reported so far with PET scintillators falls short of expectations based upon their single-photon time resolution. We characterized a 104x104 mm$^2$ HRPPD coupled to LYSO crystals and read out through a custom high-frequency amplifier. With a 2x2x3 mm$^3$ LYSO crystal we measured a CTR of 107 ps full width at half maximum (FWHM) against a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM)-based reference detector. After subtracting the calibrated reference detector's contribution of 42 ps, the single HRPPD detector was found to contribute 98 ps, corresponding to 139 ps for two identical HRPPD detectors in coincidence. With clinical 3x3x20 mm$^3$ crystals the CTR against the reference SiPM detector was 160 ps, corresponding to 218 ps for two identical HRPPD detectors. Timing and gain were uniform across output pads within measurement precision. Summing the four pads under a 3x3x10 mm$^3$ LYSO crystal, the energy resolution for 511 keV gamma ray was 14.6% FWHM, and the 1275 keV line of the $^{22}$Na source was within 1% of its proportional position relative to the 511 keV peak. Flood maps resolved the individual 3 mm elements of a 4x4 array despite the 25 mm pad pitch. To the best of our knowledge the observed timing resolution improves substantially on what has been reported for large-area MCP-PMTs coupled to PET scintillators, and the crystal array identification has not been demonstrated before on such a device. These results indicate that this device class deserves renewed consideration as a photodetector technology for high-performance TOF-PET systems.

title: Physics-based simulation unlocks scaling laws for generalizable MRI reconstruction
summary: Deep-learning-based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction holds great promise for accelerating acquisitions, yet its clinical translation remains bottlenecked by poor generalizability across unseen scanners, populations, anatomies, and protocols. Gathering sufficiently diverse clinical datasets to overcome this bottleneck is hindered by high acquisition costs, privacy restrictions, and institutional biases. Here, we introduce Scalable Inverse Model (SIM), a framework that systematically co-designs physics-simulated training data, model architecture, and learning paradigms around scalability--leveraging compute scaling to overcome historical data bottlenecks and achieve robust zero-shot MRI reconstruction. Across 14 public and in-house datasets--spanning seven international centers, five vendors, field strengths of 0.3-7 T, over ten anatomical regions, more than ten acquisition protocols, downstream quantitative and molecular tasks, and a 150-scan blinded radiologist study--SIM demonstrates robust zero-shot generalizability, recovering fine anatomical details while suppressing aliasing artifacts where conventional deep-learning methods fail. Attention-map analyses confirm that SIM learns physically explainable, dynamically adaptive reconstruction primitives rather than anatomy-specific priors. SIM establishes a scalable, privacy-preserving, and democratized infrastructure for universal MRI reconstruction, providing a blueprint for generalizable AI across inverse problems in medical imaging.

title: Towards dense optical communications with partially coherent light: I. Bimodal Stokes communications
summary: In conventional optical multiplexing, $N_{\mathrm{f}}$~orthogonal spectral or spatial modes multiplex $N_{\mathrm{f}}$ independent data streams transmitted over an optical channel (e.g., a multimode optical fiber supporting $N_{\mathrm{f}}$~guided modes). We introduce here a new optical communications scheme that we call `Stokes communications' (S-Comm), whereby $N_{\mathrm{D}}=N_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}-1$ independent data streams are multiplexed into $N_{\mathrm{f}}$~optical modes, potentially yielding a dramatic increase in the channel capacity. Rather than modulating the amplitude of each mode to encode a data stream, we make use of multimode partially coherent light and modulate each generalized Stokes parameter in the $N_{\mathrm{f}}\times N_{\mathrm{f}}$ Hermitian coherence matrix associated with the field. We present here designs for the S-Comm transmitter and receiver making use of bimodal fields ($N_{\mathrm{f}}=2$) in which $N_{\mathrm{D}}=3$ data streams are encoded via on-off keying and multiplexed in two modes. We describe the main blocks in the S-Comm transmitter: coherence modulators that encode a data stream in the degree of coherence of a bimode (a two-mode partially coherent field), Stokes encoders that assign each data stream to a prescribed Stokes parameter, and Stokes multiplexers that combine bimodes into physical modes. We also describe the reverse operations implemented in the S-Comm receiver to recover the data streams. Significantly higher channel capacity is expected for a larger number of physical modes, which is facilitated by the amenability of the presented designs to on-chip integration. These results suggest that the long-appreciated but unexploited higher information-carrying capacity of partially coherent light can help realize dense optical communications.

title: Development and Experimental Characterization of a Compact $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O Photoneutron Source for Low-Energy Nuclear Recoil Calibration
summary: Calibrating the few-keV nuclear-recoil response of liquid xenon detectors calls for a low-energy neutron source. We have developed and characterized a $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O photoneutron source that converts the 2.615~MeV $γ$ rays from $^{208}$Tl into sub-MeV neutrons through the D($γ$,n)p reaction. After optimizing the D$_2$O geometry to balance neutron production against escape efficiency, we validated the chosen configuration experimentally. The forward emission rate is $1734 \pm 76~(\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 65~(\mathrm{sys.})~\mathrm{h}^{-1}$, and the spectrum unfolded from Bonner sphere data is concentrated at $0.17$--$0.22~\mathrm{MeV}$. In a 220~h exposure of PandaX-20T, the same configuration should provide about 1000 selected nuclear-recoil events. These results support the use of a long-lived $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O source for low-energy neutron calibration of large liquid xenon detectors.

title: FGCARL: Fisher-Guided Continuously Adaptive Representation Learning for Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Deep learning (DL) has achieved remarkable success in medical image segmentation by learning data-driven representations from large-scale annotated datasets. However, medical images are often collected independently across clinical sites, resulting in substantial domain shifts due to differences in imaging modalities, acquisition protocols, and intensity distributions. Meanwhile, segmentation classes may vary across sites due to differences in annotation standards, leading to class shifts. These evolving domains and class definitions can substantially degrade segmentation performance on newly encountered data, while sequential adaptation may cause catastrophic forgetting of knowledge acquired from previously encountered domains and classes. Existing incremental learning methods for medical image segmentation primarily address either domain shifts or class shifts, with these two settings largely investigated independently. This separation leaves a critical gap in developing a unified approach that can simultaneously adapt to evolving domains and newly introduced classes while retaining previously acquired knowledge. To address this challenge, we propose Fisher-Guided Continuously Adaptive Representation Learning, a unified framework for domain- and class-incremental 3D volumetric medical image segmentation. FGCARL comprises two key components: Mutual Adaptive Instance Representation (MAIR), which adaptively aligns feature distributions across sequentially encountered domains through bidirectional normalization and denormalization, and Fisher-Guided Knowledge Retention (FGKR), which selectively preserves parameters important for previously learned domains and classes through Fisher-guided regularization. Experimental results demonstrate that FGCARL consistently outperformed state-of-the-art methods, effectively adapting to domain and class shifts while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.

title: Towards dense optical communications with partially coherent light: II. Multimode Stokes communications
summary: Partially coherent light has a higher informational-carrying capacity than coherent light when both fields are spanned by the same modes, which implies that partially coherent light may increase the channel density in optical communications. A partially coherent field spanned by $N_{\mathrm{f}}$ modes can multiplex $N_{\mathrm{D}}=N_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}-1$ data streams in the generalized Stokes parameters that uniquely identify its coherence matrix -- a scheme we call `Stokes communications' (S-Comm). We have proposed in an accompanying paper a realization of S-Comm for bimodal fields $N_{\mathrm{f}}=2$ that multiplex $N_{\mathrm{D}}=3$ data streams. Here we extend this proposed strategy for S-Comm to multimode fields $N_{\mathrm{f}}>2$. We find that the diagonal and off-diagonal Stokes parameters require different treatments and we provide detailed designs for the transmitter and receiver for both diagonally and off-diagonally multiplexed data streams. The building blocks of the proposed system can be readily implemented in integrated photonic circuit platforms. Our results indicate that on-chip processing of multimode partially coherent light (or `structured coherence') may have profound implications for optical communications and for optical signal processing in general.

title: Progress on the MALTA CMOS Sensor: Edge-TCT Measurements for Parametric Pixel Simulation
comment: 34th International Workshop on Vertex Detectors (VERTEX2026), 20-24 July 2026, in Stoos, Switzerland
summary: MALTA2 is a monolithic active pixel sensor, developed in the 180 nm CMOS imaging technology for radiation-hard applications in high-rate environments. This contribution summarizes recent developments in the characterization and simulation of MALTA2. The charge collection of a sensor on epitaxial silicon is studied with the Edge Transient Current Technique (Edge-TCT), using a digital readout, where the charge is reconstructed solely from binary hit data. In previous works, only specially designed analog output pixels at the matrix periphery were investigated. In contrast, the digital readout gives access to the full edge of the pixel matrix. Laser scans across neighboring pixels enable a two-dimensional parameterization of the charge collection. This parameterization serves as input to a parametric pixel simulation, which has been developed for chip design optimization and system-level studies. The simulation results are validated with test beam data.

title: CODE-PIF: Convex/Deep (CODE) Multiview Pseudoinvariant Features for Multitemporal Multispectral Surface Reflectance Imagery
summary: Multitemporal multispectral surface reflectance imagery exhibits radiometric and spectral variability due to atmospheric effects, sensor differences, and actual surface changes, complicating the identification of pseudoinvariant features (PIFs). The SOTA DeepMGCCA captures nonlinear dependencies across acquisition dates, but similarity in its learned feature space does not directly establish consistency in the original reflectance domain. Meanwhile, we believe that the PIFs extracted by DeepMGCCA preserve essential structural characteristics, providing an effective prior to guide subsequent refinement. Therefore, we propose the CODE-PIF architecture, an unsupervised convex/deep (CODE) framework that refines the coarse PIF from DeepMGCCA using convex optimization. Specifically, CODE-PIF uses the data-fitting term to integrate reflectance deviations, correlation-weighted spectral angles, and temporal reference change information to promote radiometric and spectral consistency between predicted PIFs and observed data. Moreover, the regularization term uses a mathematically simple Q-quadratic norm to incorporate information from the coarse PIF estimate into the refined solution. The resulting convex optimization problem is solved using the ADMM optimizer, which decomposes it into simpler subproblems and provides convergence guarantees under standard assumptions. Experiments across four distinct ROIs show improved average radiometric and spectral agreement relative to DeepMGCCA.Averaged across these regions, the RMSE decreases from 0.0192 to 0.0164, PSNR increases from 35.91 to 37.44 dB, and the between-date spectral angle decreases from 3.77 to 2.97 degrees. Although structural similarity and Pearson correlation do not improve in every scene, the results suggest that using observed data helps select PIFs with more consistent reflectance values and spectral shapes across dates.

title: Metasurfaces with Anisotropic Electric and Magnetic Conductivities: Parameter Retrieval for Arbitrary Incidence and Polarization
summary: Metasurfaces come in a great variety of unit cell geometries and material composition. A common approach for describing them relies on retrieving effective surface parameters (e.g., electric and magnetic conductivities) from plane-wave scattering data. Conventional retrieval methods are often limited to isotropic unit cells, a uniform host material, or lead to increased complexity by requiring reflection and transmission coefficients from both sides of the metasurface. Here, we derive analytical expressions for the equivalent surface conductivities of an electrically- and magnetically-polarizable anisotropic metasurface under oblique plane-wave incidence with arbitrary polarization. The proposed formulation does not require bidirectional scattering information, thus simplifying the process especially in experimental studies. The method is validated through representative electric and magnetic meta-atoms at microwave and THz frequencies, respectively. Their ability for polarization conversion is demonstrated and discussed relying on the physical insight provided by the retrieved anisotropic conductivities. In addition, we present the inverse expressions for calculating the reflection and transmission coefficients from known surface conductivity tensors, which can prove useful for metasurface synthesis and radiation problems.

title: Development of a Cryogenic Anti-Coincidence System Based on Scintillating Crystals Read Out with Kinetic Inductance Detectors for BULLKID-DM
summary: The BULLKID-DM experiment has been proposed to search for WIMP-like dark matter particles with a mass of 1 GeV or lower and with a WIMP-nucleon interaction cross section down to $10^{-43}$ cm$^2$. To achieve this goal, the experiment utilizes a detector consisting of a stack of 16 silicon wafers instrumented with phonon-mediated superconducting Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs), to be operated at the underground facility of the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS), Italy. To reduce the residual background arising from $γ$-rays, neutrons, and muons, a cryogenic active anti-coincidence system (veto) operating at mK temperature, surrounding the main detector, is under development. The veto detector consists of segmented scintillating crystals read out by phonon-mediated KID light detectors. Current status and future developments of the veto system are presented. In particular, we focus on cryogenic tests of both bismuth germanate (BGO) and gadolinium aluminum gallium garnet (GAGG) crystals, which had been previously chosen as veto candidate crystals according to our preliminary studies on the dependence of their optical properties (i.e. light yield and scintillation decay time) on temperature. We finally present the operation and preliminary tests of a two-module veto prototype with multiplexed readout.

title: Transmission-Mode Multispectral Imaging for Estimation of Microcystis spp. Cell Concentration and ELISA-Equivalent Microcystin Concentration in Water
comment: 30 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables. Includes Supplementary Information
summary: Harmful algal blooms dominated by Microcystis spp. threaten freshwater systems through proliferation and microcystin (MC) production. Conventional measurements of cyanobacterial abundance and MC concentration commonly require laboratory processing, specialized instrumentation, or assay reagents. Because MC concentration cannot always be reliably inferred from cell abundance, complementary optical approaches for estimating both quantities are of interest. This study proposes and evaluates a transmission mode multispectral imaging (MSI) framework for estimating Microcystis spp. cell concentration and ELISA-equivalent MC concentration from culture derived dilution samples. A custom built MSI system acquiring twelve spectral bands from near-ultraviolet to near-infrared wavelengths measured transmitted light spectral responses. Following principal component analysis based dimensionality reduction, spectral variation was quantified using an aggregated Wasserstein distance descriptor for regression based prediction. Cell concentration estimation yielded $R^2=0.9819$ for calibration and $R^2=0.9754$ on held-out intermediate dilution levels, while ELISA-equivalent MC estimation yielded $R^2=0.9788$ for calibration and $R^2=0.9786$ on held-out intermediate dilution levels. These results demonstrate the feasibility of transmission-mode MSI as a dual output optical calibration framework for estimation of Microcystis spp. cell concentration and ELISA-equivalent MC concentration in water.

title: Subpicosecond Optical Time Transfer under Simulated Motion with Electro-Optic Frequency Combs
summary: Extension of high performance optical frequency comb-based time transfer to real-world systems is challenged by platform motion, particularly for large relative velocities. Here, we utilize agile electro-optic frequency combs to construct a laboratory-based simulator of a two-way optical time transfer system under motion. Through direct control of the electro-optic frequency comb parameters, we can artificially induce the effects of relative motion. We performed tests of the time transfer performance across a km-scale fiber link for velocity profiles that linearly increase from rest up to 400 m/s. Through a post-processed data analysis, we demonstrate continuous tracking of the clock offset between sites with subpicosecond precision throughout the velocity sweep. These results illustrate the versatility of using electro-optic frequency combs for optical time transfer in deployed systems.

title: Adaptive carrier signal synthesis for frequency-division multiplexed cryogenic detector readout
summary: Frequency-domain multiplexing is a fundamental technology for readout of cryogenic detector arrays on a single transmission line. Synthesizing a large number of static carrier tones for resonator stimulation eventually drives the cryogenic low-noise amplifier beyond its P1dB, introducing detector signal distortion. Scaling array sizes to O(10^6) detector pixels therefore demands minimizing the total power on the transmission line by continuous tracking of the resonances, which requires the readout electronics to be capable of updating the carrier tones dynamically. This work presents an scalable FPGA-based implementation for carrier signal synthesis based on a numerically controlled oscillator and a polyphase filter bank, enabling real-time frequency adaptivity as well as frequency resolution of 4 mHz to precisely tune the operating point, while simultaneously reducing resource usage compared to the current memory-based implementation.

title: Data Archive for 2D and 3D Electrical Impedance Tomography with moderate conductivity contrast phantoms
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures. Data available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24120439
summary: This document describes open Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) measurement data that were collected from biomedical imaging inspired phantoms with moderate conductivity contrasts. The data were collected with the KIT4 and KIT5 EIT measurement devices at the University of Eastern Finland, and are intended for EIT image reconstruction algorithm development and testing. The data from thoracic imaging inspired cylindrical and chest-shaped phantoms are suitable for 2D algorithms, and the data from an intracerebral hemorrhage imaging inspired head-shaped phantom with resistive skull are suitable for 3D algorithms. In addition to the measurement data, computational meshes and example reconstruction codes are provided and sample reconstructions included.

title: Intense and stable second-harmonic generation in robust MePEA-based quasi-2D halide perovskite crystals
summary: Quasi-2D halide perovskites offer a unique platform for nonlinear optics applications, where structural and optical properties are tuned by the variation of organic spacer cations. Notably, quasi-2D perovskite single crystals can demonstrate intense and stable second-harmonic generation signals when a proper composition is selected. Here, the influence of phenethylammonium and 4-methyl-2-phenylethylammonium spacers on the crystal symmetry and second-harmonic signal response of quasi-2D perovskite phases with a varying number of single-octahedron [PbX$_6$]$^{4-}$ layers ($n$) is investigated. High-quality perovskite crystals with lateral dimensions of several hundred micrometers are fabricated using a cavity-confined crystallization synthesis method. Optical characterization of the crystals shows strong and temporally stable second-harmonic generation. Power-dependent and polarization-resolved measurements confirm the second-order nonlinear origin of the observed response and reveal anisotropic emission patterns. Our results demonstrate a direct correlation between spacer-induced center-symmetry breaking and nonlinear optical activity. These results establish quasi-2D halide perovskites as a promising class of symmetry-engineered materials for efficient frequency conversion and integrated nonlinear photonics.

title: The Gator low-background spectrometer: readout upgrade and photomultiplier tube radioassay for XLZD
summary: We report on a readout upgrade of Gator, a low-background high-purity germanium spectrometer operated at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso for material radioassay. The upgraded data acquisition records digitised waveforms, enabling noise rejection on an event-level basis, and offline energy reconstruction. Measurements before and after the upgrade show an improved energy resolution of 17% at the 2614.5 keV line of 208-Tl, with (2.14 +- 0.22) keV at FWHM, and suppression of electronic noise in the low-energy region. We assess the resulting sensitivity for a specified sample geometry, and present a new background measurement. The background rate in the (100-2700) keV range is (86.6 +- 0.5) counts/(kg day). We also show the radioassay results of sixteen Hamamatsu R17317 3-inch photomultiplier tubes with an improved stem design, which reduces the activities from the primordial 238-U and 232-Th chains by a factor of three, making them suitable candidate photosensors for the XLZD experiment.

title: Efficient refractive-index sweeps in the discrete dipole approximation using shifted Krylov methods
summary: The discrete dipole approximation (DDA) is a flexible numerical method for simulating electromagnetic scattering by particles of arbitrary shape and internal structure. In many applications, such as optical-database generation, the same particle geometry must be simulated for many values of the complex refractive index, which are currently handled independently with proportional increase of computational time. For homogeneous particles, however, variations of the refractive index affect only the diagonal polarizability term of the interaction matrix. The corresponding linear systems therefore differ only by scalar shifts of the identity matrix, making them suitable for shifted Krylov-subspace methods. In this work, we use a shifted Krylov solver adapted to the complex-symmetric formulation of the matrix and implement it in the ADDA code. The method is evaluated for a homogeneous spherical particle over a two-dimensional domain of complex refractive indices. The shifted solver reproduces the extinction cross sections obtained from independent simulations with relative differences below the iterative-method tolerance, while reducing the number of matrix-vector products by a factor of 130 for the tested configuration. We further analyze how the achievable speedup depends on the number of refractive-index values, the computational backend, and the variation of the convergence rate across the parameter space. The final wall-time acceleration for large refractive-index sweeps was demonstrated to be up to 40 times, which can be further improved by optimizing the scattered-fields calculations that became a new bottleneck.

Through direct control of the electro-optic frequency comb parameters, we can artificially induce the effects of relative motion. We performed tests of the time transfer performance across a km-scale fiber link for velocity profiles that linearly increase from rest up to 400 m/s.
